slice.question: For one ordinary post-discover client request, are the 2026-07-28 client-context metadata defaults attached to the request before transport.send at the pinned rust-sdk commit?

verified.discover_success_seeds_peer_defaults: discover_startup stores the selected protocol version plus the client's Implementation and ClientCapabilities in Peer::client_request_metadata before returning Modern and before serve_inner begins.
verified.concrete_ordinary_request: Peer<RoleClient>::call_tool_once constructs ClientRequest::CallToolRequest with default extensions and calls Peer::send_request, so its default path uses PeerRequestOptions::no_options().
verified.metadata_attached_before_queue: send_request_with_option_and_subscription mutates the request before queueing it: when client_request_metadata is present it calls set_protocol_version, set_client_info, and set_client_capabilities on request.get_meta_mut(); only afterward does it send PeerSinkMessage::Request through the peer channel.
verified.same_mutated_request_reaches_transport: serve_inner receives PeerSinkMessage::Request { request, id, ... }, wraps that same request in JsonRpcMessage::request, and immediately passes it to transport.send.
verified.default_post_discover_result: Therefore the no-options call_tool_once request after successful modern discover carries io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion and io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities, plus clientInfo, in request metadata before transport.send. This is source-level pre-transport proof at the pinned commit.
verified.direct_path_refinement: serve_directly_with_ct invokes RoleClient::configure_direct_peer; when supplied peer_info is protocol 2026-07-28 or newer, that path also seeds the same client_request_metadata defaults. With absent or older peer_info, it does not.

scope_guard: Positive evidence is limited to source-level control flow at the pinned commit and the concrete no-options call_tool_once path after a successful modern discover. It does not prove deployed-server behavior, authentication, ChatGPT connector exposure, actual bytes observed on a network, or callers that supply PeerRequestOptions.meta. Because explicit options.meta is extended after defaults, override behavior remains outside this positive scope.
